chunks: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdullah, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about a man who fasted the month of Ramadan while traveling. He said: 'If he had not received the news that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) forbade that, then there is no qada (making up) upon him, and the fasting has sufficed for him.'

Al-Sheikh (may Allah have mercy on him) said: And the limit of travel in which qasr (shortened prayer) is obligatory is two bari'd, and they are twenty-four miles. (647) 22. To indicate this is what was narrated - Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fadhal from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran from Safwan ibn Yahya from 'Isa ibn al-Qasim from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: 'In qasr, its limit is twenty-four miles.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a traveler who fasts in Ramadan without knowing it is forbidden, and what is the defined distance for travel in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib* clarifies that a traveler who fasts in ignorance of the exemption is not required to perform *qada* (make-up), as the fast is deemed sufficient. It further establishes the jurisprudential threshold for *hadd al-safar* (legal travel distance) as twenty-four miles (two *bard*), a standard used to determine the validity of shortened prayers (*qasr*) and fasting exemption. This ruling highlights the Shia emphasis on *khata'* (mistake/ignorance) in mitigating religious obligations for travelers.
